title: Kissing-number bounds
summary: PackingStar recast sphere packing as a cooperative matrix-completion game and found geometric configurations that improved 15 longstanding lower bounds for kissing numbers and related spherical codes.

title: Erdős problem survey
summary: Gemini screened 700 conjectures marked open in the Erdős Problems database. Human review identified five seemingly new solutions and eight problems whose earlier solutions were hidden in the literature.

title: Unit-distance conjecture
summary: The model constructed an infinite family of planar point sets with polynomially more unit-distance pairs than the square-grid construction, disproving the prevailing asymptotic conjecture. External mathematicians checked the proof.

title: Erdős & OEIS proofs
summary: A Lean-verified proof-search agent resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 conjectures drawn from the OEIS.

title: Cycle double cover
summary: The reported proof shows that every bridgeless graph has a collection of cycles covering each edge exactly twice. Independent expositions and a Lean formalization were subsequently released.

title: Jacobian conjecture
summary: Alpöge and Claude gave a polynomial map in three variables with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant that is not invertible. The construction refutes the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension greater than two.

title: Dinitz–Garg–Goemans
summary: The model found a network in which a divisible multicommodity flow costs 58, while every unsplittable flow respecting the stated capacity margin costs at least 60. This counterexample disproves the conjectured cost-preserving rounding guarantee.

title: Crouzeix’s conjecture
summary: The manuscript proves the sharp inequality ‖p(A)‖ ≤ 2 max|p(z)| over the numerical range of every complex matrix A. This establishes that the numerical range is always a 2-spectral set.

title: Ten mathematical advances
summary: OpenAI reported ten model-assisted results across mathematics and theoretical computer science, including constructions related to non-sofic groups. The results were released together as a single, not-yet-peer-reviewed batch.

title: Sendov’s conjecture
summary: The proof establishes that every zero of a monic polynomial in the unit disk lies within distance one of a critical point. A Lean formalization was produced and Tao published an examination of the argument.

title: Zeta zeros on the critical line
summary: Claude-assisted work reportedly raised the proven lower proportion of nontrivial Riemann zeta zeros on the critical line to 67.25%. This strengthens a quantitative approximation to the Riemann hypothesis without proving it.

title: Hadamard matrix constructions
summary: The team supplied explicit ±1 Hadamard matrices for the twelve previously unresolved admissible orders below 2000, including order 668. Exact multiplication verifies each matrix, while the general Hadamard conjecture remains open.

title: OEIS conjecture campaign
summary: A multi-model campaign tested open conjectures drawn from the OEIS and reported 147 proofs or counterexamples. The study measures scalable conjecture-solving and partly overlaps the earlier DeepMind corpus.

title: Record elliptic-curve ranks
summary: Two explicit elliptic curves over the rationals were accompanied by independent rational points proving ranks of at least 30 and 31. These surpassed the previous reported rank record of 29.

title: Hopf problem on S⁶
summary: The manuscript constructs a compact complex threefold fibred by two-dimensional tori and argues that its underlying smooth manifold is S⁶. If correct, this gives the six-sphere an integrable complex structure and resolves Hopf’s 1948 problem.

title: Erdős–Rankin improvement
summary: The model found and formalized a stronger tilted residue-class construction for unusually long intervals containing no primes. The result improves a key ingredient in the Erdős–Rankin method for large prime gaps.

title: Short prime gaps
summary: The manuscript claims infinitely many pairs of primes differ by at most 186, lowering the previous unconditional bound. The result narrows the gap toward the twin-prime conjecture but does not prove a gap of two.

title: Dying percolation conjecture
summary: The project reports a proof of the dying-percolation conjecture together with a Lean formalization, turning the probabilistic statement into a machine-checkable theorem.

title: Kozma–Nitzan follow-up
summary: A follow-up project claims proofs of the remaining Kozma–Nitzan percolation conjectures and supplies Lean formalizations. It extends the preceding dying-percolation result rather than duplicating it.

title: Fermat’s Last Theorem formalization
summary: Claude and collaborators translated the classical proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem into Lean, producing a computer-checkable verification of the theorem. The mathematical result was already known; the achievement is the formalization.

title: Köthe conjecture
summary: The project reports an explicit counterexample to Köthe’s conjecture, which asks whether the sum of two nil left ideals must be nil. A Lean check accompanies the construction.

title: Navier–Stokes regularity
summary: OpenAI reported a proof addressing whether smooth three-dimensional Navier–Stokes flows can develop singularities in finite time. The claimed Millennium Prize solution remains unverified and its priority is disputed.

title: Ibragimov–Iosifescu conjecture
summary: The project claims a counterexample to the Ibragimov–Iosifescu central limit conjecture for φ-mixing sequences, showing the stated mixing assumptions do not guarantee the proposed limit behavior.
